groups.title: LPN Med Pass
groups.note: First-semester LPN medication pass: scan the patient and each medication. One PO (lisinopril, acetaminophen, Lasix, iron, cephalexin or potassium), one SubQ (insulin lispro, a different sliding scale for each patient) and one IM (ceftriaxone, vitamin B12 or Phenergan) each.

patients.name: Sam Practice
patients.title: Hypertension follow-up (PO + SubQ + IM)
patients.desc: PRACTICE patient with the nursing information shown (lisinopril PO, insulin lispro SubQ low scale, vitamin B12 IM). Use it to learn before the check-off.

patients.desc: PO furosemide (Lasix) 20 mg, SubQ insulin lispro (sensitive scale, glucose 229 = 2 units), IM ceftriaxone 1.5 g = 3 mL (ventrogluteal or vastus lateralis)

groups.title: Case Study Patients
groups.note: Patients with a built care-plan case study (see Case Studies).

patients.name: Lauren Mitchell
patients.title: Medical-Surgical Telemetry: adrenal (Addisonian) crisis in known Addison disease after viral gastroenteritis (24 h in 4-hour checkpoints)
patients.desc: Mon 0700 to Tue 0700 in seven 4-hour checkpoints: a 46-year-old teacher with Addison disease who vomited her hydrocortisone for 2 days arrives from the ED after hydrocortisone 100 mg IV and 2.5 L of fluid. Stress-dose hydrocortisone on time, a second low glucose, sodium correcting too fast (fluid change), positive then negative orthostatics, steroid insomnia and a night near-fall, falling potassium, then the oral taper, fludrocortisone restart and sick-day rules / emergency injection teaching. Includes an instructor guide with bedside-monitor settings and a debriefing.

patients.name: Marcus Delaney
patients.title: Burn ICU: 22% TBSA flame burn with smoke inhalation and burn wound sepsis
patients.desc: 3-day Burn ICU stay (arrives 0400 Monday; the student takes over at the 0700 shift change, Mon 0700 to Thu 0700): Parkland resuscitation, intubation and sedation, escharotomy, day-2 burn wound infection with sepsis and norepinephrine, extubation on day 3, transfer to Med-Surg.

patients.name: Doris Kowalczyk
patients.title: Step-Down: right hip fracture ORIF (POD 2) with a catheter-associated UTI
patients.desc: 3 shifts on the Step-Down Unit (Tue 0700 to Wed 1500): post-operative care after hip ORIF, a catheter-associated UTI recognized by new confusion and fever, treated with ceftriaxone, then transfer to a skilled nursing facility.

patients.name: Raymond Kessler
patients.title: Telemetry Step-Down: hypermagnesemia from over-the-counter magnesium with acute kidney injury on CKD, emergent hemodialysis (24 h in 4-hour checkpoints)
patients.desc: Tue 0700 to Wed 0700 in seven 4-hour checkpoints: a lethargic, bradycardic man with CKD 4 and AKI who took milk of magnesia, a Mg antacid and magnesium oxide; calcium gluconate, fluids and diuretic, deterioration with respiratory depression, emergent hemodialysis, hypoglycemia after dialysis, magnesium rebound with delirium and constipation, then recovery teaching. Includes an instructor guide with bedside-monitor settings and a debriefing.

groups.title: DKA Patients
groups.note: Seven pre-built type 1 diabetes patients in diabetic ketoacidosis, each 3 days long (Day 1 0700 to Day 4 0700). Vital signs after the 0700 arrival come from the bedside monitor (monitor.html). See casestudy/cases/DKA_SERIES.md and each patient's INSTRUCTOR_NOTES.md.

patients.name: Maya Thompson
patients.title: DKA 1 of 7, PICU to adolescent unit: new-onset type 1 diabetes in severe DKA (3 days, checkpoints every 0700 and 1900)
patients.desc: Mon 12/07 0700 to Thu 12/10 0700. A 16-year-old with 5 weeks of thirst, peeing and weight loss arrives in the PICU in severe DKA. Pediatric protocol (one 10 mL/kg bolus, insulin 0.1 unit/kg/h without bolus, two-bag dextrose, potassium and phosphate), cerebral edema signs at 1130 treated with mannitol, low potassium with U waves, DKA resolved overnight, transition to glargine and lispro, a night low after a bedtime correction, then CGM, glucagon, sick-day and school teaching with her parents. Vital signs after 0700 come from the bedside monitor.

patients.name: Jordan Ellis
patients.title: DKA 2 of 7, intermediate care to medical floor: insulin pump failure after a weekend of drinking (3 days, checkpoints every 0700 and 1900)
patients.desc: Mon 12/14 0700 to Thu 12/17 0700. A 24-year-old line cook with type 1 diabetes since age 11 wakes after a friend's birthday with his pump set half pulled out, vomits all day thinking it is a hangover and arrives in moderate DKA. Adult protocol (fluids, fixed-rate insulin 0.1 unit/kg/h, D10 line under 250, peripheral potassium riders with the insulin held for K 3.3), a regular soda he was not supposed to drink, glargine bridge and the drip off, a low after a half-eaten dinner, then the pump back on after a site-change teach-back and a kinked cannula caught overnight. Alcohol screening, withdrawal watch and safer-drinking teaching. Vital signs after 0700 come from the bedside monitor.

patients.name: Denise Carter
patients.title: DKA 3 of 7, step-down / telemetry: type 1 diabetes in DKA after months of cost-related insulin rationing (3 days, checkpoints every 0700 and 1900)
patients.desc: Mon 11/09 0700 to Thu 11/12 0700. A 38-year-old single mother who lost her insurance and rationed insulin arrives in DKA; care ends with medicines and supplies in hand. Vital signs after 0700 come from the bedside monitor.

patients.name: Marcus Reyes
patients.title: DKA 4 of 7, step-down / telemetry: type 1 diabetes in DKA with acute kidney injury on CKD G3b (3 days, checkpoints every 0700 and 1900)
patients.desc: Thu 11/05 0700 to Sun 11/08 0700. A 31-year-old with type 1 diabetes and kidney disease from birth arrives in DKA with AKI; care needs small fluids, careful potassium and a kidney-safe plan. Vital signs after 0700 come from the bedside monitor.

patients.name: Ruth Nakamura
patients.title: DKA 5 of 7, ICU: type 1 diabetes, SGLT2-inhibitor DKA with near-normal glucose, E. coli urosepsis and delirium (3 days, checkpoints every 0700 and 1900)
patients.desc: Thu 11/05 0700 to Sun 11/08 0700. A 67-year-old with type 1 diabetes on an SGLT2 inhibitor arrives confused with urosepsis and DKA although her glucose is only 210; care ends with a safe insulin plan and her daughter's teach-back. Vital signs after 0700 come from the bedside monitor.

patients.name: Samuel Okafor
patients.title: DKA 6 of 7, cardiac step-down: type 1 diabetes, DKA from a silent NSTEMI, potassium 3.3 on insulin, stent and radial hematoma (3 days, checkpoints every 0700 and 1900)
patients.desc: Mon 11/16 0700 to Thu 11/19 0700. A 45-year-old bus driver with type 1 diabetes arrives on the cardiac step-down unit in DKA from a silent heart attack; care covers the potassium drop on insulin, heparin, a stent and a driver-license worry. Vital signs after 0700 come from the bedside monitor.
